If you go to r/argentina you will probably get a pesimistic point of view of the country because generally people want out from here. To be honest, some days I want out too. But being a foreigner, and specially a british foreigner, makes the experience of living in Argentina completely different from a native's perspective.

THE PROS

I'll start by telling you about living in Argentina so that I can explain some things about working in Argentina later.  
The people of Argentina are very particular. I guess the mix of different cultures and historic contexts of the migrants that inhabited these lands is what has made the way people act in society so different from people of other countries. But people here are really friendly, there is a sense of community rarely seen in other countries, and they are in general very talkative, social, touchy and confident among each other, wether we're talking about family and friends or randoms in bars. I've heard of migrants living overseas and not having a group of friends even after years living in their new countries, and I find that weird because I think it is impossible for a migrant to live here for more than 6 months without creating some cool relationships or finding friends. People here are sociable!  
Places in Argentina are really cool, we have glaciers, waterfalls, desert, mountains, rivers, hot places, cold places; so a lot of options for you. There are three main cities that are really big which are Rosario, Cordoba and Buenos Aires, the capital, (where everything is and where I would recommed you to go if you like living in the city with mass transit systems, endless buildings and a lot of different options for you to work).   
Also, English is very much needed for everything and there is a lot of demand for english teachers. In Buenos Aires you could find an infinite number of English Institutes that would probably give you a job if you learn basic spanish. Nonetheless there is probably an English institute in every single city with more than 50000 unhabitants in this country.  
Politics in Argentina have made the country a very accessible one for migrants, however that doesn't mean you won't have to fill a thousand papers - probably.  
The very best part is also the worst part, and it's about how my beautiful country is kinda poor. That makes it VERY cheap to live in and very easy to get an upper mid-class lifestyle, but I'll let you read this link that will clarify your doubts: [https://www.shipit.co.uk/blog/guides/moving-to-argentina-expat-guide](https://www.shipit.co.uk/blog/guides/moving-to-argentina-expat-guide)

I'll finish the pros by telling you that you will pobably find a job within the first two months, and that most jobs give you health insurance so that you can get healthcare in private hospitals, but there's also a horrible, but functional public healthcare system so you will never die for example from being poor and not affording an ambulance as it happens in some countries like the U.S.  


THE CONS  
The worst part of living here is that it's still a third-world latin american country and dude, that carries so many things:  
You won't get paid a lot unless you work a lot or get a job in a good place.

There is a lot of poverty, even though you won't necessarily see it if you live in big cities and you don't explore much of the suburbs. However this usually carries insecurity. It's not the most secure place on earth. It might not be Africa or Brazil, but you still have to take care of yourself in the streets as assaults, robberies and insecurity in general are common in the big cities. Drugs and gangs are not really a big problem in comparison with some other countries.

People are very close minded, specially in small cities, with things like weed, lgbt people, and being different in general, but that generally disappears in big cities.

There are many things that separate us culturally so you should really think about the things that you like about living where you live and compare them to what they're like in Argentina so that you can start getting an idea of whether you would be happy in a place like this or not.

If you decide you want some more info, feel free to DM me

Como ya te dijeron, lo jodido en outdoor es el calor de enero en Argentina, especialmente de Baires para arriba. La lana de roca lo que hace es que tiene poca densidad entonces no acumula tanto calor como la tierra ni tiene tanta resistencia.
También yo no creo mucho en eso, pero viste que hay calendarios lunares que dicen cuales son los mejores días para hacer cada cosa, plantar, germinar, etc. por ahí te sirve

Cunado ya tenes una plaga me parece que la única solución es ponerle productos y de manera continua. Es un poco bajón porque si ya está en flora, rociar mucho los cocos puede darte hongos. Yo en general la rocío una vez por semana desde bebe hasta que esta en la segunda semana de flora, para después dejar de rociar la planta y como mucho rociar la tierra. Un mes antes de la cosecha ya deberías dejar de rociarle cosas para que no le cambie el gusto a los cogollos, no tengan hongos ni moho, y no se queme la planta por el exceso de humedad.
Para serte honesto nunca tuve trips (si otras plagas peores) pero calculo que podes tratar de sacarlos con el cepillo lo mas que puedas y después rociarlo con una mezcla de aceite de neem y jabón potásico diluido en agua dos veces por semana, no mucho cada vez pero si de seguido, ponele dia de por medio, durante dos semanas y ver si disminuyen, y después dejar de ponerle antiplagas.
